title: Build a scalar autograd engine and multi-layer perceptron from scratch
brief:
Deep learning frameworks like PyTorch and JAX operate on automatic differentiation computation graphs. To demystify these abstractions and diagnose gradient bugs with confidence, build a lightweight scalar reverse-mode automatic differentiation engine from scratch in pure Python.

Your implementation must construct a dynamic computation graph on the fly, execute reverse topological sorting, support gradient accumulation across branching nodes, and train a Multi-Layer Perceptron (MLP) on a non-linear dataset.
deliverables: A Value scalar class tracking data, grad, child references (_prev), operation name (_op), and backward closure (_backward)
Operator overloads for addition, subtraction, multiplication, division, power, negation, and activation functions (ReLU, Tanh)
A backward() method executing a depth-first search topological sort to ensure adjoint gradients propagate in exact reverse dependency order
Proper handling of multi-path graph branches using gradient accumulation (self.grad += out.grad * local_derivative) to prevent dropped gradients
Neuron, Layer, and MLP classes built on Value objects supporting parameter collection and zero_grad()
A verification test suite comparing computed gradients against PyTorch autograd tensors to within 1e-6 relative tolerance
